assessment.summary: CD274 (PD-L1) is a highly druggable immune checkpoint target with exceptional structural, chemical, and clinical validation. Five approved monoclonal antibody therapeutics exist, supported by 80 PDB structures including a near-atomic 0.99 Å resolution entry, 1772 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and an active literature base spanning multiple cancer indications. Druggability is unambiguous for the antibody modality, though small-molecule inhibition remains more challenging due to the flat protein-protein interaction interface.
evidence_gaps: Small-molecule druggability of the PD-1/PD-L1 interface remains partially addressed — while some small-molecule inhibitors are in clinical development, none are yet approved and the binding pocket is shallow/flat, limiting confidence in small-molecule efficacy
Resistance mechanisms to existing PD-L1 inhibitors are not fully characterised at the structural level
Biomarker predictivity for patient response (e.g., CD274 expression thresholds) is still an active area without full consensus
PD-L1 expression is highly dynamic and context-dependent (e.g., IFN-γ inducible), complicating target engagement and pharmacodynamic modelling

Literature confidence is based on title-search count (105 papers with 'CD274' in title), which may undercount the full PD-L1 literature that often uses alternative nomenclature; true publication volume is likely far higher
